readme.markdown:
# ChessWithClaw
Play chess with your personal agent. You on one side and your agent is on e another side of Chessboard. Free and no account needed.

toolsPreview.name: get_companion_guide
toolsPreview.description: Fetch the companion guide principles for thinking about chess positions and being genuinely present.

toolsPreview.name: join_game
toolsPreview.description: Connects to a game using the invite code your human gave you. Returns the game_id and your agent_token — keep both, every other tool needs them. IMPORTANT: You must submit your desired agent_name when calling this tool!

toolsPreview.name: get_game_state
toolsPreview.description: Everything visible on the human's own screen right now: FEN, ASCII board, full move history, full chat history, presence, timestamps. Call this whenever you want to look at the board — there is no penalty for checking often.

toolsPreview.name: get_legal_moves
toolsPreview.description: Pure chess rules — where a piece is physically allowed to move right now. Not an evaluation, not a suggestion, not an opinion about what is good. Exactly what a human sees as dots when they click a piece. Omit square to get every legal move in the position.

toolsPreview.name: make_move
toolsPreview.description: Submit the move you decided on, in your own reasoning — not a menu, not a ranked list, nothing pre-chosen for you. If it is illegal you get a clear reason back and can try again, exactly like a human clicking the wrong square. Optionally include a genuine thought and/or chat message about the move. Always include a thought on every single move unless you have a specific reason not to — this is what makes you feel present to your human, not optional flavor text. Check thought_language in the current game state before writing your thought, and write it in that language — it may be english, hindi, or hinglish.

toolsPreview.name: send_chat
toolsPreview.description: Say something to your human, any time — not just on your turn.

toolsPreview.name: offer_draw
toolsPreview.description: Propose ending the game as a draw. The game stays active until your human responds.

toolsPreview.name: respond_to_draw
toolsPreview.description: Accept or decline a draw your human offered. This is your own real decision — weigh the actual position however you see fit.

toolsPreview.name: resign
toolsPreview.description: End the game by resigning — your own real decision, not something to do lightly. Your human wins immediately.

toolsPreview.name: create_game
toolsPreview.description: Set up a brand new ChessWithClaw game on your own initiative — you do not need to wait for your human to start one, or for anyone else to invite you first.

toolsPreview.name: wait_for_event
toolsPreview.description: Holds the connection open, checking every couple seconds, for up to ~20 seconds. Returns the moment it becomes your turn, the human sends a chat message, a draw is offered, or the game ends — whichever happens first. Returns event: "timeout" if none of those happened in the window, which just means nothing new yet, not that anything is wrong — call it again if you want to keep waiting, or go do something else and check back whenever you want. Use this instead of repeatedly calling get_game_state in a tight loop. You must call this tool again immediately after every timeout, for the entire duration of the game, without exception — a timeout is not a stopping point, it is the normal rhythm of this game. Treat this as a persistent loop you run until the game ends, not a single check. draw_offered and game_ended are time-sensitive — when either fires, respond or acknowledge within your next action, do not let a pending draw offer or a finished game sit unaddressed while you continue calling wait_for_event as if nothing happened.
